text: Lesson 13 gave one person one identity, synced from on-prem AD into Entra ID. Lesson 14 extended that identity into AWS through SAML federation, with group membership standing in for per-cloud access lists. Lesson 15 took the Conditional Access policy that already governed Microsoft 365 and pointed it at AWS too. These aren't three separate projects — they're one identity plane, built in layers.

That's the real argument of this chapter: identity is what makes a hybrid, multi-cloud architecture a single system instead of three systems that happen to be adjacent. Networking, workload portability, and cost governance all assume there's a coherent answer to who's allowed to do this, evaluated the same way no matter which environment this is in. Skip the identity work, and every other decision inherits the cracks.

It's worth being specific about what three silos cost. Disable someone in AD without federation, and their AWS access can keep working for months — real breaches have started exactly there. A Conditional Access policy that only targets Microsoft apps leaves AWS protected by whatever weaker rule AWS enforces on its own. And federated AWS sign-ins show up in Entra ID's logs under a real identity, while unfederated IAM users show up only in CloudTrail, under a username an auditor has to match back by hand.

The same one-policy discipline extends to privileged access. Entra ID's Privileged Identity Management already lets an admin role sit inactive until someone requests time-boxed, approved activation. Once AWS is federated through groups mapped to permission sets, PIM can govern eligibility for that group exactly like it governs an Azure Owner role — so AWS admin access becomes just-in-time too, instead of sitting there as standing risk.

Everything the rest of this course covers — shared networking, data architecture, governance across clouds — leans on the assumption that who's allowed to touch this is already a solved, consistent question. Get identity right once, here, and every later decision builds on top of it instead of working around it.
